t: Charlemagne's Frankish empire united much of Western and Central Europe and revived the Western imperial title in 800.
Its scholars copied much of the classical Latin literature that survives today, in the new Carolingian minuscule script.
The Frankish custom of dividing realms among sons split it at Verdun in 843 and broke it apart for good by 888.
dyk: Charlemagne's silver penny, struck at 240 to the pound, was the basis of the pound-shilling-penny system used in Britain until 1971.
ev: Charles Martel checks an Umayyad raid near Tours and Poitiers
Pepin the Short deposes the last Merovingian king and is made king with papal approval
Charlemagne conquers the Lombard kingdom and becomes King of the Lombards
Basques destroy Charlemagne's rearguard under Roland at Roncevaux Pass
Pope Leo III crowns Charlemagne emperor in Rome on Christmas Day
Louis the Pious inherits the undivided empire
Treaty of Verdun divides the empire among Charlemagne's grandsons
Charles the Fat is deposed and the empire fragments permanently
